official_measurement_examples.name: Self-certification route
official_measurement_examples.fact: GOV.UK says registered installers can self-certify covered work instead of the customer making a separate Building Regulations approval application for that work.

official_measurement_examples.name: Certificate timing
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current GOV.UK guidance says the registered tradesperson should provide a compliance certificate within 8 weeks of completion.

official_measurement_examples.name: Fenestration schemes
official_measurement_examples.fact: Government scheme guidance lists authorised self-certification routes for replacement windows, doors, roof windows and rooflights within defined building scopes.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 fenestration competence
official_measurement_examples.fact: The mandatory technical competence framework published 1 July 2026 includes fenestration as a competence category.

official_measurement_examples.name: Replacement glazing history
official_measurement_examples.fact: English council guidance records replacement glazing entering Building Regulations control from April 2002, while replacement of glass alone is treated differently from replacing complete units.

official_measurement_examples.name: Ventilation preservation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Replacement-window guidance requires ventilation provision not to be made worse and Part F requirements must be met rather than deferred by disclaimer.

official_measurement_examples.name: Multiple requirements
official_measurement_examples.fact: Replacement windows can engage thermal, safety, ventilation and escape considerations; one certificate or design feature should not be treated as proof of every requirement in isolation.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Building Regulations compliance or self-certification for replacement windows and doors does not itself grant planning permission, listed-building consent or Article 4 permission where those are separately required.

core_rules: window or door self-certification is not planning permission
planning permission is not Building Regulations fenestration compliance
scheme membership is not proof of a specific installation
compliance certificate is not land-use permission
replacement glass alone must not be conflated with replacement of complete window or door units
Part F ventilation duty is distinct from Part L thermal duty
Part K safety glazing is distinct from Part L energy performance
escape-window provision is distinct from planning permission
night-vent position is not an acceptable substitute for required background ventilation
Article 4 planning control is distinct from Building Regulations self-certification
listed-building consent is distinct from Building Regulations self-certification
certificate timing is not a planning determination period
2026 MTC competence evidence is not parcel approval
replacement-window compliance does not create ownership or access rights
no parcel fenestration clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
